title: 反相比例放大器：虚短与虚断
statement: 图示为理想 op-amp（运算放大器）构成的反相比例放大器，v_s = 1 V，R_1 = 10 kΩ，R_f = 40 kΩ。
求 R_1 中的电流 i_1（参考方向见图）和输出电压 v_o（o 端对地）。

questions.explain: 虚断：流入反相端的电流为零，i_f = i_1。v_o = v_{−} − R_f·i_f = 0 − 40k × 0.1 mA = −4 V，即 v_o = −(R_f/R_1)·v_s。

questions.ask: 关于反相输入端结点 n，下列说法正确的是？
choices: n 点电位为零（虚地），但它并没有真的接地
n 点用导线接地，所以电位为零
choiceExplain: 图上 n 点并没有导线接到地。想一想：它的电位是由哪条规则决定的？
“虚短”使 v_{−} 等于同相端电位 v_{+}，而不是等于 v_s；只有 v_s 接在同相端时（同相放大器、跟随器）才有 v_{−} = v_s。看一看这里的同相端接在哪里。
questions.explain: n 点电位为零是因为“虚短”（v_{−} = v_{+} = 0），并不是真的有导线接地；正因为“虚断”，R_1 的电流不会流进 op-amp（运算放大器），只能全部经过 R_f。

hints: R_f 把输出接回反相端（负反馈），所以可以用理想 op-amp（运算放大器）的两条规则：虚短 v_{−} = v_{+}；虚断 i_{−} = i_{+} = 0。
同相端接地，所以反相端 n 也是 0 V；R_1 的电流全部流过 R_f。
solution: **1. 负反馈与虚短。** R_f 把输出接回反相端，构成负反馈，op-amp（运算放大器）工作在线性区。同相端接地，v_{+} = 0，由虚短 v_n = v_{−} = 0（虚地）。
**3. 结点 n 的 KCL。** 由虚断，反相端不取电流，所以 i_f = i_1 = 0.1 mA。
**验算：** 公式 v_o = −(R_f/R_1)·v_s = −4 × 1 V = −4 V ✓。“−”号表示输出与输入反相。

en.title: Inverting amplifier: virtual short and virtual open
statement: The ideal op-amp forms an inverting amplifier with v_s = 1 V, R_1 = 10 kΩ, R_f = 40 kΩ.
Find the current i_1 in R_1 (reference direction as drawn) and the output voltage v_o (terminal o to ground).

questions.explain: Virtual short: v_{−} = v_{+} = 0 (the non-inverting input is grounded, so the inverting input is a "virtual ground"). Hence i_1 = (v_s − 0)/R_1 = 1/10k = 0.1 mA.
Virtual open: no current enters the inverting input, so i_f = i_1. v_o = v_{−} − R_f·i_f = 0 − 40k × 0.1 mA = −4 V, i.e. v_o = −(R_f/R_1)·v_s.

questions.ask: Which statement about the inverting-input node n is true?
choices: n is at 0 V (a virtual ground), but it is not actually connected to ground
n is wired to ground, so it is at 0 V
n is at the potential v_s
choiceExplain: No wire connects n to ground in the figure. Which rule fixes its potential?

The virtual short makes v_{−} equal to the non-inverting input v_{+}, not to v_s; v_{−} = v_s only when v_s drives the non-inverting input (non-inverting amplifier, follower). Look at where the non-inverting input is connected here.
questions.explain: n is at 0 V because of the virtual short (v_{−} = v_{+} = 0), not because of a wire to ground. Because of the virtual open, the current in R_1 cannot enter the op-amp and must all flow through R_f.

hints: R_f connects the output back to the inverting input (negative feedback), so the two rules of the ideal op-amp apply: virtual short v_{−} = v_{+}; virtual open i_{−} = i_{+} = 0.
The non-inverting input is grounded, so node n is at 0 V too; all of R_1's current goes on through R_f.
solution: **1. Negative feedback and the virtual short.** R_f connects the output back to the inverting input: negative feedback, so the op-amp works in its linear region. The non-inverting input is grounded, v_{+} = 0, so by the virtual short v_n = v_{−} = 0 (virtual ground).
**3. KCL at n.** By the virtual open the inverting input draws no current, so i_f = i_1 = 0.1 mA.
**Check:** the formula v_o = −(R_f/R_1)·v_s = −4 × 1 V = −4 V ✓. The minus sign means the output is inverted.
